text:
The story in Vancouver is who wants to be there for what comes next. Jake DeBrusk "still refuses to be part of a Canucks rebuild," per Markerzone, and Heavy.com says his fate with the team is "All But Officially Sealed." Elias Pettersson is the subject of sell-high talk, too: Yahoo Sports asked whether now is "The Right Time For The Canucks To Sell High On Elias Pettersson."

The record explains why. The Canucks are 3-16-1 with 7 points, winless in six (0-6-0) and 1-9-0 over their last ten, outscored 25-13 during the skid. They take only 39.9 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances), so the slide is real. But it's also been made worse. Their goalies have allowed 14.75 more goals than the shots deserved, and Kevin Lankinen is at .802 with 9.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts (0-5-0). Our numbers say their play has earned about 14 points.

Monday's 3-1 loss to Philadelphia at least showed a pulse in the third period, when Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored on a line with Pettersson and Brock Boeser. Liam Öhgren is running hot with 4 points in 10 games. Our simulations give them no real playoff chance and project about 60 points. What to watch now is the trade market, and whether the goaltending stops making a bad team look worse than it is.
headline: A rebuild nobody fully signed up for
